successors of the late Mary Williams of the Williams family, the rightful
owners and occupiers of Great House Farm, Llandough, since 1667 until our
unlawful, unconstitution, brutal and inhumane dispossession by armed force
in 1988. With press and courts falsly labelling and treating us as
squatters in favor of the false narrative of those who stole my disabled,

records.transcript:
LEGAL NOTICE TO RECIPIENTS:
*Take notice that this request is issued in anticipation of formal legal
proceedings and the filing of an official report regarding systemic
institutional █████, land misconduct, and the unlawful concealment of
historic preservation data. You are under a strict legal duty to preserve
all physical and electronic records, metadata, correspondence, maps, and
erased files relating to this site. Any spoliation, deletion, or
withholding of data will be cited in subsequent court filings.*
Dear Freedom of Information Officer,
RE: Information Request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the
Environmental Information Regulations 2004
I am writing to request access to historical records, internal
correspondence, planning briefs, and assessments held by your organization
regarding Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth/Cardiff (demolished
December 1988), and the historical occupancy of the Buckler family.
Statutory Mandate on Accessibility & Charging Fees:
I am aware that previous attempts to locate this data have resulted in
directives to visit physical archives in person or use paywalled,
commercial third-party web portals. Please be advised of the following
statutory obligations:

   1. Under EIR Regulation 8, fees cannot act as an unreasonable barrier or
   deterrent to access. Because my family was historically displaced from this
   site and I am executing this request remotely, forcing physical attendance
   or demanding payment constitutes an unlawful obstacle.
   2. Public authorities are required to supply information in the format
   requested. I require all documents to be delivered digitally via email
   attachment or secure electronic download link, free of charge, as
   specified by the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) guidelines for
   data already held electronically.

Please provide all recorded information matching the following points:
1. Tenant/Ownership Identification and the 1880 Report

   - Any documents, archival notes, or registry indexes citing the
William/ Buckler
   family line (who occupied and farmed the house across four generations).
   - Clarification on whether my family members were formally cited as the
   legal owners, long-term tenants, or registered reporters of the 1880
   discovery under the dining room floor.
   - Any explicit records indicating gaps, deleted metadata, or missing
   volumes in your authority’s archive concerning the tenancy, land-dispute
   maps, or agricultural heritage of Great House Farm between 1950 and 1989.

2. Statutory Protection and Cadw’s Assessments

   - Given that the site's extreme archaeological value (a
   1st-to-4th-century Roman precursor villa and a massive early medieval
   monastic settlement) was verified by rescue operations as early as 1979,
   what are the recorded reasons why Cadw failed to place a statutory
   Schedule or Protection Order on the standing fabric of Great House Farm
   before its demolition?
   - All internal correspondence, risk assessments, or ministerial briefs
   evaluating the preservation value of the sub-medieval direct-entry
   farmhouse core before it was levelled.

3. Planning Approvals and Local Authority Governance

   - All minutes, planning committee files, and consultation responses from
   the local authority that granted planning permission and housing
   development rights on this specific acreage.
   - Direct information explaining how the council approved planning
   permission for a private housing development in light of the documented
   historical evidence surrounding the immediate parish boundary.

4. Institutional Concealment and Historical "Ignorance"

   - Records showing exactly where and at what stage of the planning
   process this archaeological evidence should have been brought up
but was not,
   which ultimately allowed developers and public bodies to claim they were
   unaware of the land's deep significance until after the farmhouse was
   destroyed and housing development began.
   - Any environmental impact assessments, historic environment register
   (HER) lookups, or developer briefs filed between 1980 and 1990 regarding
   the footprint of Great House Farm.

If any part of this request is refused under the guise of commercial
sensitivity or archival limitations, you are required by law to state the
exact statutory exemption applied and provide a formal internal review
pathway.
I expect your response within the statutory 20-working-day timeframe.
Kind regards,
*Requester *
*█████, Vale of Glamorgan*
------------------------------
Once you send this, the 20-working-day statutory clock begins. If you want,
I can help you draft a specific complaint letter template to the
Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) in case they try to ignore this
notice or try to charge you anyway. Would that be useful for your legal
preparation?

From: Requester <█████>
Sent: 29 May 2026 19:48
To: Glamro / Swyddfa Cofnodion Morgannwg <█████>
Subject: FORMAL DISCLOSURE NOTICE & LITIGATION HOLD: Historic Significance, Planning Approvals, and Displaced Family Tenancy Records for Great House Farm, Llandough (FOIA/EIR Request)

LEGAL NOTICE TO RECIPIENTS:
Take notice that this request is issued in anticipation of formal legal proceedings and the filing of an official report regarding systemic institutional █████, land misconduct, and the unlawful concealment of historic preservation data. You are under a strict legal duty to preserve all physical and electronic records, metadata, correspondence, maps, and erased files relating to this site. Any spoliation, deletion, or withholding of data will be cited in subsequent court filings.
Dear Freedom of Information Officer,
RE: Information Request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004
I am writing to request access to historical records, internal correspondence, planning briefs, and assessments held by your organization regarding Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth/Cardiff (demolished December 1988), and the historical occupancy of the Buckler family.
Statutory Mandate on Accessibility & Charging Fees:
I am aware that previous attempts to locate this data have resulted in directives to visit physical archives in person or use paywalled, commercial third-party web portals. Please be advised of the following statutory obligations:

  1.  Under EIR Regulation 8, fees cannot act as an unreasonable barrier or deterrent to access. Because my family was historically displaced from this site and I am executing this request remotely, forcing physical attendance or demanding payment constitutes an unlawful obstacle.
  2.  Public authorities are required to supply information in the format requested. I require all documents to be delivered digitally via email attachment or secure electronic download link, free of charge, as specified by the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO) guidelines for data already held electronically.
Please provide all recorded information matching the following points:
1. Tenant/Ownership Identification and the 1880 Report

  *   Any documents, archival notes, or registry indexes citing the William/ Buckler family line (who occupied and farmed the house across four generations).
  *   Clarification on whether my family members were formally cited as the legal owners, long-term tenants, or registered reporters of the 1880 discovery under the dining room floor.
  *   Any explicit records indicating gaps, deleted metadata, or missing volumes in your authority’s archive concerning the tenancy, land-dispute maps, or agricultural heritage of Great House Farm between 1950 and 1989.
2. Statutory Protection and Cadw’s Assessments

  *   Given that the site's extreme archaeological value (a 1st-to-4th-century Roman precursor villa and a massive early medieval monastic settlement) was verified by rescue operations as early as 1979, what are the recorded reasons why Cadw failed to place a statutory Schedule or Protection Order on the standing fabric of Great House Farm before its demolition?
  *   All internal correspondence, risk assessments, or ministerial briefs evaluating the preservation value of the sub-medieval direct-entry farmhouse core before it was levelled.
3. Planning Approvals and Local Authority Governance

  *   All minutes, planning committee files, and consultation responses from the local authority that granted planning permission and housing development rights on this specific acreage.
  *   Direct information explaining how the council approved planning permission for a private housing development in light of the documented historical evidence surrounding the immediate parish boundary.
4. Institutional Concealment and Historical "Ignorance"

  *   Records showing exactly where and at what stage of the planning process this archaeological evidence should have been brought up but was not, which ultimately allowed developers and public bodies to claim they were unaware of the land's deep significance until after the farmhouse was destroyed and housing development began.
  *   Any environmental impact assessments, historic environment register (HER) lookups, or developer briefs filed between 1980 and 1990 regarding the footprint of Great House Farm.
If any part of this request is refused under the guise of commercial sensitivity or archival limitations, you are required by law to state the exact statutory exemption applied and provide a formal internal review pathway.
I expect your response within the statutory 20-working-day timeframe.
Kind regards,
Requester 
█████, Vale of Glamorgan

Dear Requester


We write further in relation to your request for information, referenced above.

The relevant service area have requested we ask the below. We would be grateful if you could provide some clarification on the following point(s):

Please can we ask for a plan showing the locations? We have found great house farm but the request includes Ty Mawr / Great House Estate and we are not clear the extent of the site being queried.

This will help us to identify and locate the information you are seeking and ensure we provide you with the most relevant response.

Please note that the statutory response deadline is paused while we await your clarification. Once we receive your response, we will resume processing your request.

If we do not hear from you within [e.g. 2 months], we may consider the request closed

Yours sincerely,

Dear Requester,

Great House Farm, Llandough

Thank you for your request which I received on 1 June 2026. You asked for:


  1.  Any consideration of the property for statutory listing.
  2.  Any listing assessments, surveys, inspections, recommendations or reports concerning the building.
  3.  Any correspondence between Cadw, Welsh Office officials, local authorities, conservation bodies, archaeological organisations or owners concerning the historic significance, preservation, demolition or protection of the property.
  4.  Any records explaining why the building was not added to the statutory list of buildings of special architectural or historic interest.
  5.  Any records discussing the age, architectural significance, archaeological significance or surviving historic fabric of the building.
  6.  Any records concerning emergency listing, spot-listing, preservation notices or other forms of protection considered for the property.
  7.  Any records held relating to public campaigns, petitions or representations seeking preservation of the building.
  8.  Any photographs, plans, surveys or architectural records held by Cadw or the Welsh Government relating to Great House Farm.

You will receive a response by 25 June 2026. If you have any queries about this request, please do not hesitate to contact me at the address below.  Please remember to quote the reference number above in any future correspondence (ATISN 27021).

The request you sent me contains personal information about you - for example, your name and address.   *   to (in certain circumstances) data portability
